objectives.text: Keep Faustin-Archange Touadera in power. He was expected to win a third term at the December 2025 election after a 2023 referendum removed the term limits (AP, pre-vote explainer, Dec 2025). The result is not verified in this pass.

means.text: Foreign forces as the regime's guard. Russian advisers have operated since March 2018 (free military aid, widely believed to be Wagner); Africa Corps was to replace Wagner in 2026 (Touadera in Moscow in March 2026 to finalise it; the USD 15m a month figure has one source only and is not used). A bilateral Rwandan force has operated since 2020 outside MINUSCA; the government said both countries sent hundreds of troops after an alleged coup bid. Rwanda is also among the largest MINUSCA contributors.

constraints.text: The UN scaffolding is shrinking. MINUSCA was extended for a year, but the Security Council said its presence would scale down because of budget constraints (AP, as summarised in search results). Its own troop mix is led by Rwanda and Bangladesh, so the UN is not an independent guard.

paradoxes.text: The guard that keeps Touadera in power makes him dependent on the patrons who take the minerals. The government's own account of the foreign deployment is an alleged coup bid that it blamed on former president Bozize's backing of militias (Naharnet); the threat it names is what keeps the guards in place.

sources.title: C. Africa Says Russian, Rwandan Troops Sent after Alleged Coup Bid

grand_strategy.reading:
Bangui's strategy is regime survival through foreign guards: Russian advisers since 2018 and a Rwandan force since 2020 hold the capital and the state, while Touadera seeks a third term under a constitution changed in 2023. The price is minerals, and the mission that is meant to hold the peace, MINUSCA, is itself led by Rwanda and shrinking for budget reasons. France has left, so the choice is Moscow or Kigali, and both of those patrons are paid in the same ground that the armed groups fight over.
Not verified for this card: the armed-group field (the CPC coalition has no source here, so no stance or actor file was written for it), the Chad and Sudan border and RSF spillover, diamond and gold export volumes, and the French aid resumption of 2024-25.

stances.note: Bangui agreed in March 2018 to Russian military aid; the advisers are widely believed to be Wagner, which has operated in the country since 2018, and Touadera went to Moscow in March 2026 to finalise the move to Africa Corps (one outlet, unconfirmed on the figure). No treaty text was found, so 'ally' is our reading of a stable de facto alignment with a patron that guards the regime (C). Bond none: the sources show a security exchange, no kinship or affinity named. Trend stable: the change of name from Wagner to Africa Corps is continuity, not a turn. Mirror: the RUS card holds no stance toward CAF, so the build's provisional reciprocal is only a placeholder; Moscow's own grade should be written from its side. Gap: the gold and timber concessions are not sourced in this pass.

stances.note: The brief framed Rwanda as a partner; the RWA card's own reading is a bilateral security guarantee, outside MINUSCA, protecting the Touadera government, and a stance that follows that structure rather than the troop count is an ally (de facto alignment). Recorded as ally at C, not partner: a deliberate departure from the brief, to be confirmed. Rwanda confirmed its soldiers were deployed but gave no figures; Kagame said the force acts under a bilateral arrangement, not UN rules of engagement (AP summary, search results). Bond none: no kinship or affinity named. Gap: troop numbers and the text of the bilateral agreement are not found.
